blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, the word that best describes a serious company's relationship with its taxes is stewardship. The company is not simply a payer; it is a steward of a quiet relationship with every country in which it operates — built across decades, strengthened by honest behaviour and weakened by careless conduct. Governments change, ministers change, rules change — but the company's record does not.

The senior leader who understands this makes tax decisions with a longer horizon than the next quarter. An aggressive interpretation that wins a small saving today, at the cost of trust tomorrow, is a poor trade. A cautious interpretation that concedes a modest amount but keeps the relationship clean is usually, across five or ten years, the cheaper path.

The stewardship view does not mean paying more than you owe. It means paying exactly what you owe, paying it calmly, and protecting the kind of long-term reputation that is very hard to rebuild once it has been spent.

items.q: According to the text, what best describes a serious company's relationship with its taxes?
items.why: "the word that best describes a serious company's relationship with its taxes is stewardship."

items.q: What does the stewardship view say a company should pay?
options: More than it owes, to be safe
As little as the law can be read to allow
Whatever preserves the current quarter's result
items.why: "It means paying exactly what you owe" — nem mais, nem menos.

items.q: The author suggests that an aggressive interpretation is a poor trade because…
options: the small saving today costs trust tomorrow
items.why: "An aggressive interpretation that wins a small saving today, at the cost of trust tomorrow, is a poor trade."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Trust with a tax authority is built over many years.
A small tax saving is worth pursuing even if it damages a long relationship.
Reputation is very hard to rebuild once lost.
Tax decisions should look beyond the next quarter.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta o oposto — a economia pequena não compensa o dano à relação.

items.q: The phrase "Governments change, ministers change, rules change — but the company's record does not" suggests that…
options: the company should ignore changes in the law
its past conduct outlasts the officials it dealt with
reputations are easily reset with each new government
items.why: Inferência: o histórico da empresa permanece e é lembrado, mesmo quando as pessoas e regras mudam.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James contestando uma posição fiscal agressiva numa reunião de comitê. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Before we vote on this, I want to be honest about what we're actually weighing. The saving on the table is real, but it's small — a fraction of a single quarter's result. And to get it, we'd be taking an interpretation the authority has never accepted, on a matter we've handled cleanly for twenty years.

I've sat across the table from these people. When a filing is straightforward, they wave it through. The moment they sense we're being clever, every future return gets read line by line. That scrutiny doesn't cost us in this quarter — it costs us for a decade.

So my recommendation is that we concede the point. Pay exactly what a reasonable reading says we owe, no more, and keep the relationship clean. I'd rather give up a modest amount now than spend the next ten years explaining ourselves. Reputation with a revenue office is the one asset we can't buy back once we've spent it — and no one in this room will thank us for a saving nobody remembers.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does James describe the size of the potential saving?
options: Large enough to justify the risk
Small — a fraction of a single quarter's result
Equal to a full year's tax bill
items.why: "the saving on the table is real, but it's small — a fraction of a single quarter's result."

items.q: What does James say happens once the authority senses the company is "being clever"?
options: They read every future return line by line
items.why: "The moment they sense we're being clever, every future return gets read line by line."

items.q: What is James's actual recommendation to the committee?
options: Take the aggressive position and defend it later
Delay the decision to another quarter
Concede the point and pay exactly what a reasonable reading says they owe
Pay more than they owe to reassure the authority
items.why: "my recommendation is that we concede the point. Pay exactly what a reasonable reading says we owe, no more."

items.q: What does James imply by saying the scrutiny "costs us for a decade"?
options: The damage is spread over years, not confined to one quarter
The saving will only appear after ten years
The authority takes a decade to respond
The company must reorganise every ten years
items.why: Inferência: ele contrasta o ganho de um trimestre com um custo que se estende por muitos anos.

items.q: What is the underlying attitude behind James's argument?
options: He wants to avoid all tax obligations
He values a durable relationship over a short-term gain
He is indifferent to the outcome
items.why: Inferência: ele prioriza a reputação de longo prazo — 'the one asset we can't buy back' — acima da economia imediata.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board treats its tax record as a matter of stewardship." Stewardship here means…
options: responsible care of something entrusted to you over time
items.why: Stewardship = zelo / custódia: cuidar responsavelmente de algo que lhe foi confiado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A senior leader makes tax decisions with a longer ___ than the next quarter."
items.why: Horizon = horizonte temporal; o líder olha além do próximo trimestre.

items.q: "We chose the cautious interpretation and kept the relationship clean." Cautious means…
items.why: Cautious = cauteloso, prudente — o oposto de agressivo.

items.q: Choose the correct verb: "I'd rather ___ a modest amount now than damage a twenty-year relationship."
items.why: To concede = ceder; abrir mão de um ponto para preservar algo maior.

items.q: "Reputation is very hard to rebuild once it has been spent." To rebuild means to…
items.why: To rebuild = reconstruir; recuperar algo que foi perdido ou danificado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre postura fiscal. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on the tax position." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "James pushed back on the aggressive interpretation." This means he…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "A small saving today won't move the needle on our long-term standing." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer uma diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We agreed to be conservative, but the desk never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "An aggressive filing can come back to haunt you years later." This means it can…
options: cause serious problems in the future
items.why: Come back to haunt you = voltar para te assombrar; causar problemas mais adiante.
